content.intro: This lesson develops topic 207 of the supplied curriculum: **F2PY and Fortran Interoperability**. The main starting point is **What F2PY does**. You will connect the idea to a small, synthetic example, then use the result to reason about shape, dtype, accuracy, or memory as appropriate.
content.why_it_matters: Compiled extensions and stride-level operations can improve specialized workloads but increase portability and memory-safety complexity. Learn the high-level array contract first and keep extension paths narrowly tested.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Treat **F2PY and Fortran Interoperability** as an explicit step in an array workflow. This lesson centers on **What F2PY does** and the source syllabus's related subtopics. Before trusting a result, identify the input shape and dtype, perform the smallest useful operation, and inspect the output. The example uses synthetic data so you can change one value and observe what changes.

content_blocks.code:
# PowerShell / terminal command (run only when a Fortran source is available):
python -m numpy.f2py -h example.pyf example.f90
content_blocks.expected_output: F2PY inspects the Fortran file and writes a signature file; compilation requires a compatible compiler toolchain.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Run the PowerShell/terminal command from the project environment. The F2PY command additionally requires an available Fortran source and a compatible compiler.
content_blocks.reset_steps: For examples that create files, use a temporary working directory and remove its outputs after reviewing them. The memory-map example already uses a temporary directory.

content_blocks.title: Guided walkthrough
content_blocks.text: F2PY can generate wrappers for supported Fortran routines, but compilation requires an available compatible compiler. Treat it as an optional compiled-extension track.

common_mistakes.problem: Using low-level memory tools without validating strides and bounds
common_mistakes.why: Strided views and extension interfaces depend on layout and ownership contracts.
common_mistakes.fix: Start with safer high-level functions and add targeted tests before low-level paths.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming compiled binaries work across major NumPy versions
common_mistakes.why: The C API has binary-compatibility concerns across major versions.
common_mistakes.fix: Build/test wheels against supported NumPy versions and review migration notes.
